phase: live Ghidra machine-contract reconstruction, clean-room model, and focused x86-32 model verification
target_state: staged candidate source; runtime validation gated

implementation.port_policy: No port was needed. The body makes no call other than the single tail jump to 0x00951240, reads no global and writes no memory. No global, service or type record was created.
implementation.state_policy: No state is written anywhere. The receiver is only tested (TEST ECX,ECX) and offset (LEA EAX,[ECX+imm]); it is never dereferenced for a store. The model test asserts this by memcmp over the whole receiver before and after driving all six keys through both entry points.
implementation.naming_policy: The entry symbol is named set_image_009817c0 because that is the name the reconstruction queue record requires in order to bind this source span to VA 009817c0. It is a binding label, not a description: the observed body is not a setter and takes no image pointer. See contradiction sdk-name-is-not-the-observed-behaviour.
implementation.clang_format_pointer_alignment_reason: The validator resolves the source span with a regex that admits the return type only as a single unspaced token, so PointerAlignment: Right would reformat the bare return type from void* to 'void *' and yield zero function spans for this VA. Left alignment keeps the bare type spelling void* intact and clang-format --dry-run -Werror clean at the same time.

return_sites: 0x009817f1: RET 0x4 (null result, shared by both null guards and by the fallthrough)

ordinary_stack_arguments.name: hash
ordinary_stack_arguments.role: 32-bit comparison key, tested against four CMP immediates and never masked, widened or used as an index

observed_original_abi.return_type_rationale: The machine level fact is that EAX is the exit register and that the value in it is a pointer: either the receiver itself, the receiver offset by a proven member displacement (0x04 or 0x0c) taken by LEA EAX,[ECX+imm], or the null produced by XOR EAX,EAX. The return type is declared void* because the evidence proves a pointer is returned but does NOT prove any declared pointee type: the receiver is only tested and offset, never dereferenced for a typed load. This contradicts the imported Ghidra prototype, which claims void; see contradiction ghidra-prototype-is-impossible.
observed_original_abi.return_semantics: Returns the address of the member selected by the hash argument relative to the receiver: receiver + 0x04 for hash 0xeec58382, receiver + 0x0c for hash 0xeef3af8c, receiver + 0x04 for hash 0xee3f516e, the bare receiver for hash 0x6ec581fd, and null for any other hash. Both locally handled offsets and the delegated 0x04 offset are null-guarded; the bare-receiver 0x6ec581fd case is NOT null-guarded and returns the receiver verbatim even when it is null.
observed_original_abi.return_observation: EAX is written on every path. The three null exits materialise it with XOR EAX,EAX, the two local offset exits with LEA EAX,[ECX+0x4] and LEA EAX,[ECX+0xc], and the delegated paths by the tail-called 0x00951240, whose own exits are ADD EAX,0x4 and XOR EAX,EAX. So the returned value is always a deliberate pointer result, not a residual register.

prototype_rejected.reason: The imported prototype declares two ordinary stack arguments, which under a callee-cleaned convention would require RET 0x8. The body ends with RET 0x4 in all three of its return sites and reads only entry_ESP+0x4, so the machine contract is a single-argument callee. The imported prototype is not the machine contract and is not used here.

observed_mechanics: MOV EAX, dword ptr [ESP + 0x4] at 0x009817c0: the only argument read is the single 4-byte word at entry_ESP+0x4, loaded into EAX and used solely as a comparison key.
CMP EAX, 0xeec58382 at 0x009817c4 then JZ 0x009817e5: the first key, routed to the +0x04 arm.
CMP EAX, 0xeef3af8c at 0x009817cb then JZ 0x009817db: the second key, the only one this target adds over its tail-call target, routed to the +0x0c arm.

MOV dword ptr [ESP + 0x4], EAX at 0x009817d2: a store of EAX into the very slot EAX was loaded from at 0x009817c0. It is semantically a no-op on the argument and exists only to keep the argument live across the tail call.

JMP 0x00951240 at 0x009817d6: a tail call, not a CALL. There is no return address pushed and no stack adjustment, and the receiver is still in ECX because the preceding MOV dword ptr [ESP + 0x4], EAX left ECX untouched. Every key this target does not handle locally is delegated with the same receiver and the same key.
TEST ECX, ECX at 0x009817db and 0x009817e5: each local arm null-guards the receiver before offsetting it.
LEA EAX, [ECX + 0xc] at 0x009817df and LEA EAX, [ECX + 0x4] at 0x009817e9: the two proven member displacements, 0x0c and 0x04, as the only pointer arithmetic in the body.
XOR EAX, EAX at 0x009817ef: the shared null result, reached from both null guards and from neither local arm otherwise.
RET 0x4 at 0x009817e2, 0x009817ec and 0x009817f1: all three exits pop the one 4-byte argument, so stack cleanup is 4 bytes owned by the callee.

The body never stores to memory other than the redundant argument slot at entry_ESP+0x4, never dereferences the receiver, and contains no CALL and no absolute address, so it is a leaf with no global reference.
The target's own CFG has three basic blocks and two conditional edges, and its only outgoing edge other than the two RETs is the tail jump to 0x00951240.

Raw bytes at 0x009817c0..0x009817f3 are 8b4424043d8283c5ee741a3d8caff3ee740989442404e965fafcff85c974108d410cc2040085c974068d4104c2040033c0c20400, read twice and independently: once through the live Ghidra bridge and once by a direct byte scan of SPORE/SporeBin/SporeApp.exe, whose sha256 is 25d42a7a5c4d438fb155233230f57d29e2849bfdff5c889a5d0847f0469d914e. The two agree byte for byte.

semantic_findings.statement: 0x009817c0 is not a setter. It maps a 32-bit comparison key and a receiver address to the address of one of that receiver's members, and returns null for any key it does not recognise. The combined key-to-offset table reachable through this entry point is 0x6ec581fd -> +0x00, 0xee3f516e -> +0x04, 0xeec58382 -> +0x04, 0xeef3af8c -> +0x0c, anything else -> null.
semantic_findings.evidence: ghidra_disassemble_function 0x009817c0; ghidra_disassemble_function 0x00951240; the four CMP immediates and the three LEA/ADD displacements across both bodies

semantic_findings.statement: 0x009817c0 is a strict superset of the table implemented by its tail-call target 0x00951240. The target handles 0xeec58382 -> +0x04 and 0xeef3af8c -> +0x0c itself and delegates everything else. 0x00951240 handles 0x6ec581fd -> +0x00, 0xee3f516e -> +0x04 and 0xeec58382 -> +0x04. The two tables agree on 0xeec58382, and the target is the only place 0xeef3af8c and the +0x0c displacement appear, which is why the tail call cannot be treated as an opaque fallback.
semantic_findings.evidence: ghidra_disassemble_function 0x009817c0 and 0x00951240 compared instruction by instruction

semantic_findings.statement: The 0x6ec581fd arm of 0x00951240 branches straight to its RET with EAX still holding the receiver, so a null receiver yields a null result there by accident of the value rather than by a guard. The 0xee3f516e and 0xeec58382 arms of the same function, and both arms of 0x009817c0, are preceded by an explicit TEST ECX,ECX. This asymmetry is reproduced by the model and asserted by the test.
semantic_findings.evidence: 0x0095124c JZ 0x0095126e targets the RET directly and skips every TEST; contrasted with 0x0095125e and 0x00951268

semantic_findings.statement: The little-endian pointer 0x009817c0 occurs exactly twice in the whole image, both in .rdata, at 0x01441a50 and 0x01444880. Those are vtable slots, so the function has no direct caller and is reached only by virtual dispatch. The two xrefs the bridge reports as calls are in fact this-adjusting thunks: 0x00969b40 is SUB ECX,0x4 followed by JMP 0x009817c0, and 0x00969b50 is SUB ECX,0xc followed by JMP 0x009817c0. Both subtract a member offset from the receiver before re-dispatching on the same key, which independently corroborates that the values this function returns are member offsets.

The little-endian pointer 0x00951240 occurs exactly once in the image, in .rdata at 0x01445c10. So the function this target tail-calls is itself reached through a vtable, which is consistent with a family of resolver virtuals rather than a private helper. The base of the table containing 0x01445c10 was not determined and no slot index is claimed for it.

Across both modelled entry points and all six keys exercised, the receiver is only tested and offset. The single store in the body, MOV dword ptr [ESP + 0x4], EAX, targets the caller's argument slot and not the receiver. The model test asserts this behaviourally with a memcmp over the whole receiver.
semantic_findings.evidence: ghidra_disassemble_function 0x009817c0; test_receiver_is_never_written in the focused model test

vtable_slot_observations.slot_delta: +0x84 from slot 0 at 0x014447fc; the complete-object-locator word sits at 0x014447f8
vtable_slot_observations.table_shape: Slots 0 through 27 are the repeated value 0x011e06d0, except slot 2 which holds 0x006ae1f0. Slots 28 onward are distinct UTFWin code addresses: 0x00984a30, 0x00836470, 0x00982770, 0x00969b40, 0x009826e0, 0x009817b0, 0x00980320, 0x009800e0, 0x009838e0, 0x009817c0, 0x00982780.
vtable_slot_observations.note: 0x00969b40 in slot 31 is the SUB ECX,0x4 / JMP thunk that targets this function, so a table can carry both the resolver and the this-adjusting thunks into it.

vtable_slot_observations.slot_delta: +0x20 from slot 0 at 0x01441a30; the complete-object-locator word sits at 0x01441a2c
vtable_slot_observations.table_shape: Slots 0 through 7 are 0x00805630, 0x00982760, 0x00969b50, 0x0096ff50, 0x00981860, 0x00980320, 0x009800e0, 0x009838e0. The three words 0x00980320, 0x009800e0 and 0x009838e0 are shared with the 0x014447f8 table, so the two tables overlap on a common interface prefix.
vtable_slot_observations.note: The ASCII string ConsoleWindow begins at 0x01441a70, immediately after the last slot read here. It is an adjacent symbol, not a proven class name for this table, so no class identity is asserted from it.

vtable_family_layout_evidence.observation: Both vtables that contain the target place 0x009838e0 in the slot immediately below it, and both contain the triple 0x00980320, 0x009800e0, 0x009838e0. The 0x01441a2c table places 0x00969b50 in slot 2 and the 0x014447f8 table places 0x00969b40 in slot 31; those two addresses are the this-adjusting thunks into this function.
vtable_family_layout_evidence.not_established: Which C++ class owns either table, and which interface the target's slot belongs to. SporeApp.exe carries no MSVC RTTI, so class identity cannot be read from the binary.

codegen_equivalence.method: clang++ -m32 -std=c++17 -O2 -c, then objdump -d of the emitted .text body compared against the original bytes read from SporeApp.exe
codegen_equivalence.release_o2_difference: clang at -O2 inlines the tail call, so the sibling's three extra keys are folded into the same body, and it reassociates the four equality tests into a two-way branch on hash > 0xeef3af8b with a shared ADD/LEA block and a CMOVNE for the two null guards. The original instead keeps the tail call, keeps a flat chain of CMP/JZ pairs, and branches on TEST ECX,ECX. The comparison immediates 0xeec58382, 0xeef3af8c, 0xee3f516e and 0x6ec581fd, the displacements 0x4 and 0xc, the RET 0x4 exits and the null-pointer materialisation are all present in the emitted body; only the shape of the decision tree differs.
codegen_equivalence.release_o2_semantic_equivalence: Established behaviourally rather than by byte comparison, by test_differential_against_transcription, which drives the model and an independent flat transcription of the disassembly over the same 142 keys against both a live and a null receiver and requires identical results.
codegen_equivalence.debug_O0_difference: clang at -O0 emits an unoptimised frame with a stack probe call, spilled locals and calls to the add_offset helper, so byte correspondence is not claimed at -O0.

notes: Each test seeds the receiver with a distinct byte pattern and asserts that no word of it changes under any key, so an invented store would abort.
The comparison-key boundaries are asserted explicitly at each constant and at constant-1 and constant+1, because an off-by-one in a CMP immediate would survive a random sweep.

test_differential_against_transcription embeds a second, deliberately flat transcription of 0x009817c0 written straight from the listing, sharing no helper and no control structure with the model, and requires the two to agree on 142 keys against both a live and a null receiver.
clang-format --dry-run -Werror is clean over all three sources against the .clang-format staged with the package.

The package stages its own .clang-format with PointerAlignment: Left instead of copying the sibling packages' Right. The reason is recorded in implementation.clang_format_pointer_alignment_reason: the resolver admits a return type only as a single unspaced token, so a spaced spelling silently produces zero function spans and the record drops to NOT_AVAILABLE even though every line of it is correct.

live_provenance.analysis_basis: Read-only live Ghidra MCP queries plus a direct byte scan of SPORE/SporeBin/SporeApp.exe, language x86:LE:32, image base 0x00400000. No Ghidra mutation and no save was performed this attempt.
live_provenance.analysis_basis_note: The SDK import name is a candidate label only. Every immediate, displacement, register, width and RET form recorded here was read from the machine body. The vtable slot indices were obtained by scanning the whole image for the little-endian pointer and locating each hit relative to the surrounding table, and the resulting slot addresses were cross-checked against the bridge with a targeted read_memory.
tools_used: direct byte scan of SPORE/SporeBin/SporeApp.exe for 0x009817c0 and 0x00951240

contradictions.summary: The queue record and the Spore-ModAPI import both name this address UTFWin::ScrollbarDrawable::SetImage. The body is not a setter: it returns a pointer, takes one 32-bit comparison key instead of an index and an image pointer, and writes nothing at all. A SetImage that stores an image into a scrollbar would have to write through the receiver. No reading of the machine makes this a setter.
contradictions.consequence: The reconstruction models the observed behaviour and keeps the queue-mandated symbol name set_image_009817c0 only so the validator can bind the span. No semantic claim is made that this is UTFWin::ScrollbarDrawable::SetImage.

contradictions.summary: The imported prototype is void UTFWin::ScrollbarDrawable::SetImage(IScrollbarDrawable *this, int index, Image *pImage). Two ordinary stack arguments under callee cleanup would require RET 0x8, but all three exits of the body are RET 0x4 and the body reads only entry_ESP+0x4. The declared return type void is also contradicted by the fact that EAX is written with a pointer on every path. The machine contract is a single-argument callee returning a pointer in EAX; the imported prototype is rejected.

The bridge decompilation of this address renders the argument as IScrollbarDrawable *this and compares that pointer against the constants 0xeec58382 and 0xeef3af8c, and it discards the EAX results of the LEA and XOR instructions. The persisted export .spore-analysis/ghidra-exports/decompiled_sdk/UTFWin__ScrollbarDrawable__SetImage.c carries the same wrong output. The decompiler is mis-typing a uint32 key as the receiver pointer because the imported prototype forces a receiver-typed first parameter. The reconstruction is based on the disassembly and the raw bytes, never on that decompilation.

The briefing and ghidra_get_xrefs_to report an out-edge from 0x009817d6 to 0x00951240 as a direct-call, and report 0x00969b43 and 0x00969b53 as UNCONDITIONAL_CALL xrefs to this function. All three are JMP instructions, not CALL. The full-image pointer scan finds the target in exactly two places, both vtable slots, so the function has no direct caller at all.

unresolved_questions: Which C++ class owns vtables 0x01441a2c and 0x014447f8, and which interface is the target's slot a member of? SporeApp.exe carries no MSVC RTTI, so class identity cannot be recovered from the binary. The adjacent ASCII string ConsoleWindow at 0x01441a70 is an adjacent symbol, not a proven class name for either table.

What generates the four constants 0x6ec581fd, 0xee3f516e, 0xeec58382 and 0xeef3af8c? They are used only as equality keys in these two bodies, and whether they are hashes of type names, field names or something else is not observable here.

What are the declared names and types of the members at +0x00, +0x04 and +0x0c of the receiver? The offsets are proven by the LEA and ADD displacements, but nothing in either body dereferences a typed field, so no field name or type is recoverable from this target alone.

Is the base of the vtable containing 0x00951240 at 0x01445c10 identifiable, and does that table share an interface with the two tables that contain this target? Only the single pointer occurrence is established; no slot index is claimed for it.

Why does the 0x6ec581fd arm return the receiver without a null guard while every other arm is guarded? The asymmetry is observed and reproduced, but whether it is intentional in the original source or an artefact of how the resolver was generated is not determinable from the machine.

Is the MOV dword ptr [ESP + 0x4], EAX at 0x009817d2 an artefact of the original build's tail-call lowering, or an explicit argument write in the source? It is a semantic no-op on the argument either way, so the model does not depend on the answer.
runtime_gates: No original-process invocation and no indirect-caller trace was captured, so no concrete caller and no real key value are known. The key-to-offset table is proven from the two bodies but the values a real caller passes, and therefore which members these offsets name, cannot be observed without a trace.
The owning C++ class name and the interface identity of the target's vtable slot are not established, because SporeApp.exe carries no MSVC RTTI.
The member names and declared types behind offsets +0x00, +0x04 and +0x0c are not established; only the offsets themselves are proven.

The provenance of the four comparison constants is not established, so it cannot be checked whether another translation unit contributes further keys to the same table that are unreachable from this entry point.

ports_and_runtime_gates.port_rationale: The body makes no CALL other than the single tail jump to 0x00951240, which is modelled in the same package because it is required to reproduce the delegated keys. No external service, host call or global is referenced, so no port was created.

scope.package_scope: The single assigned VA. 0x00951240 is modelled in the same translation unit as a required dependency of this target's tail call and is NOT promoted to a record of its own. The this-adjusting thunks 0x00969b40 and 0x00969b50, the sibling slots of the two vtables and the vtable pointer occurrence of 0x00951240 were read as evidence only and were not promoted.

corrections_to_prior_record.previously_claimed: The package is clang-format clean against the sibling staging packages' .clang-format, which uses PointerAlignment: Right.
corrections_to_prior_record.corrected_finding: The package ships its own .clang-format with PointerAlignment: Left, so the return type stays spelled void*.
corrections_to_prior_record.why_changed: The first version of this package used PointerAlignment: Right, which reformatted the return type to a spaced spelling. check_span.py then reported "the source artifact opens but no function span binds to this VA" with zero spans found, because the resolver regex admits the return type only as a single unspaced token. Aligning the format config with the resolver is the fix that keeps both the bare type spelling and clang-format cleanliness.
corrections_to_prior_record.impact: Span binding and the ABI/RETURN SEMANTICS comparison both pass, and the sidecar return_type now compares equal to the span return type instead of warning.
